correctness.rationale: For independent local depolarization the Pauli string of weight j decays at j*gamma. On trace-one states the full Poisson reset adds r(rho_D-rho); solving each coefficient gives x/(x+j), including the preserved identity, and uniqueness for r>0. Independent symbolic reproduction (independent_pt.py, Python 3 and SymPy) sums signed Pauli expectations on the six computational Dicke components; only weights 0, 2 and 4 survive. Partial transpose on the leading k qubits negates precisely the strings with an odd number of Y factors there. With Q=(x+2)(x+4), automatic component factorization of the two exact matrices scaled by 12Q gives all factors and multiplicities in RESULT.md §§2–3. In particular, for k=1 the possibly negative scaled roots are 6-9x-6x^2=3(x+2)(1-2x) once and 6-x twice; the remaining linear roots and both roots of the quadratic are positive for x>0. For k=2 the possible negative scaled roots are 6-7x-4x^2 twice and 6-4x-2x^2=2(1-x)(x+3) once. In each sector the residual quadratic has two real roots (Hermiticity), positive root sum and strictly positive product for x>0. Dividing by 12Q and summing negative magnitudes checks both negativity laws. Negative counts are 0/1/3 on (0,1/2], (1/2,6], (6,infinity), and 0/2/3 on (0,beta], (beta,1], (1,infinity), where 1/2<beta=(sqrt(145)-7)/8<1. This verifies the half-open cut-dependent window, including the zero eigenvalues at transition points. Symmetry gives four cuts of type 1|3 and three of type 2|2. The unreset limit is I/16 and the pure-state limits give negativities 1/2 and 5/6. This proof establishes PPT and NPT, not separability of PPT cuts or a multipartite entanglement classification.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Both weight sectors are present, so a common white-noise amplitude cannot reproduce the reset path at finite positive x. A fixed depolarization time is not an equivalent reparametrization either: time attenuation obeys (weight-two factor)^2=weight-four factor, whereas [x/(x+2)]^2<x/(x+4).

value.rationale: Equal noise on all sites need not produce the same PPT behavior on cuts of different sizes. This exact stationary example identifies the sharp interval where all one-versus-three cuts are NPT but every balanced cut is PPT, and locates additional inertia changes invisible to a single witness. The resource state and channel are independently motivated; the full cut-resolved profile is useful for comparing robustness in this reset model without claiming separability or multipartite entanglement beyond the spectral conclusions.
